summary: Talhar Airport (BDN/OPTH) is a small airfield located in the Badin District of Sindh province in southeastern Pakistan, near the Indus River delta region. Originally developed as a military airstrip, it now serves limited civil aviation purposes for the surrounding agricultural and coastal areas. The airport primarily supports occasional charter flights, pilot training, and emergency operations rather than scheduled commercial service.
faqs:
Q: Does Talhar Airport have scheduled commercial flights?
A: No, the airport does not currently offer scheduled commercial passenger service. It is primarily used for occasional charter, private, and training flights.

Q: What is the airport mainly used for today?
A: It serves general aviation needs including pilot training, charter operations, and occasional government or emergency flights serving the Badin District.

Q: Is the airport open to international flights?
A: No, Talhar Airport is a domestic small airfield without customs or immigration facilities, so international flights are not accommodated.

Q: What is the nearest major airport with commercial service?
A: Jinnah International Airport (KHI) in Karachi is the closest major international airport, located approximately 200 km to the west-northwest of Talhar.
transport_tips: Getting to Talhar Airport typically requires a private vehicle or taxi from Badin city, as there is no public transit directly serving the airfield. The drive from central Badin takes roughly 20-30 minutes depending on road conditions. Travelers should arrange ground transport in advance, as ride-hailing apps have very limited coverage in this rural area of Sindh.
local_tip: Visitors should carry sufficient water and sun protection, as the Badin District experiences extremely hot and humid weather for much of the year, and airport facilities at Talhar are minimal with no on-site concessions or shaded waiting areas.
